subject.title: File Browser: Remove ALLOWED_FILE_NAMES whitelist, add scope levels

question: Should OpenClaw add workspace-wide and/or system-wide file browsing through Gateway and Mission Control, and what permission boundary should replace the current allowlist?
rationale: The request changes which files operator clients can read or write and crosses a deliberate allowlist boundary added after an arbitrary workspace-read security bug.

options.title: Approve workspace-only API first
options.body: Land or redesign the workspace-scoped `agents.workspace.*` path with explicit read/admin scopes, path safety, size limits, and UI proof while deferring system filesystem access.

options.title: Keep bootstrap-only files
options.body: Leave `agents.files.*` restricted to MC/bootstrap files until a stronger product case and security model exists.

options.title: Approve system scope design
options.body: Open a separate security-reviewed design for host filesystem browsing with explicit operator opt-in, read/write limits, auditing, and recovery UX.

recommendation.title: Approve workspace-only API first
recommendation.body: Land or redesign the workspace-scoped `agents.workspace.*` path with explicit read/admin scopes, path safety, size limits, and UI proof while deferring system filesystem access.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history shows direct involvement in the relevant file-read boundary and gateway refactor path.
